changes: Item drops now favor gear near the level of the monster you killed, instead of always dropping the same item regardless of zone
Fixed freshly bought/dropped/claimed gear showing as "Lv 1" instead of its real level
Hunter Hats and Coats now cap at level 120, matching the rest of Hunter's armor progression
Fixed a bug where armor (rings, necklaces, boots, hats, coats) could be equipped into the weapon slot instead of showing as not wearable yet
Equipped gear now leaves your Inventory and shows only in the Equipment tab, freeing up the slot it used to take
The Shop now shows your Inventory alongside its buy screens, and gear can be sold there for gold
Combat rewards (gold, EXP, item drops, Meteors, DragonBalls) are now verified by the server instead of trusted from your device, paving the way for future player trading
Added Loot Holding — a new storage area for item drops that couldn't fit in your Inventory, so nothing gets lost while combat resolves in the background
Replaced the placeholder EXP curve with real leveling data, capped at level 130
Fixed a bug where Wuxia characters dealt 0 damage in combat
Combat damage now factors in the enemy's Defense instead of ignoring it entirely
Renamed the Warehouse's account-wide currency section to "Bank" for clarity
Meteors and DragonBalls can now drop from kills (Meteors are rare, DragonBalls are very rare), instead of only being obtainable through manual testing
Offline progress now includes any Meteors/DragonBalls earned while you were away
Level Upgrade in the Forge now advances an item to the next real item in its line (e.g. a low-level Ring becomes the next Ring up), instead of just bumping a number with no effect
Warehouse: gear can now be dragged out to withdraw it, and stones can be dragged in to deposit them, matching how dragging already works everywhere else
Fixed Warehouse currency withdrawals appearing to vanish — Meteors and DragonBalls wallet balances now show alongside the bank amount
Completely renamed all 8 zones and their monsters (Windhollow, Cinderleaf, Stormvale, Sunscar Wastes, Talon Isle, Duskspire Keep, Twistpath Ruins, Rimehollow) with fresh names and rebalanced stats
All 8 zones are now unlocked and playable, not just 3
Monster names now show in white, green, red, or black depending on the level gap between you and them
Killing a much higher-level monster now grants bonus EXP; killing one you've heavily outleveled grants much less
Shop now has Weapons and Armor tabs alongside Arrows, showing gear you can buy with gold
The Weapons/Armor lists are dynamic — they only show gear your class can actually use
Added a real gear catalog: 117 new items across Bows, Rings, Necklaces, Boots, Archer Hats, and Archer Coats (levels 1-130)
Archer Hats and Coats now require the Hunter class
Quality upgrades (Tempered/Infused/Radiant/Ascended) now actually make gear stronger, not just change its name/color
Warehouse: merged the Gold/Meteors/DragonBalls and Composition Stone deposit rows into the single "Account Wide Deposits" card instead of three separate sections

Warehouse redesign: renamed "Currency" to "Account-Wide Warehouse", removed the per-row balance counters, and added a single "Deposited Totals" summary showing Warehouse Points and your Gold/Meteors/DragonBalls bank amounts
Warehouse Storage now sits above your Inventory in one column, with the new summary alongside them
Equipment page and Combat page now show your character's name instead of a level counter / "Your HP" label
Forge: removed the Meteors/DragonBalls summary card, and the Forge controls now sit side-by-side with your Inventory instead of stacked
Warehouse: Meteors and DragonBalls now show as "Inventory" instead of "Wallet", matching how Composition stones are already described
Warehouse: deposited stones and composed gear now convert into Warehouse Points, a shared balance you spend to withdraw any tier back — no longer locked to the exact tier you deposited
Monsters now fight back! You have your own HP shown on the Combat page, above the enemy — getting knocked out stops the fight and fully heals you
Combat page: Zone and Monster are now simple dropdowns with one Fight button, instead of a separate zone-button row and enemy list
Equipment page: removed the placeholder character silhouette and the equipment icon row up top, and made the remaining gear slots bigger
Added the Warehouse — a new tab for storing extra gear, Composition stones, and currency
Gear and stones are stored per character (each character has its own Warehouse, with its own 40-slot capacity, separate from your Inventory)
Gold, Meteors, and DragonBalls are stored in a shared account-wide bank — deposit from any character, withdraw into any other
Lucky Arrow stacks are now 10 gold instead of 150
Enemy roster no longer shows HP/gold/EXP up front — just the monster name
Inventory tiles, and the Forge's Upgrade Slot and Fuel slots, are now a consistent, smaller size
Renamed the game from Greybox Idle to Ascension Idle
Added real zones and monsters: Dual Town, Waterbird Fortress, and Monkey Town are now selectable, each with their own enemy roster — 5 more zones are visible but locked, coming soon
Your Inventory now lives on the Combat page instead of the Equipment page, so you can manage gear without leaving a fight
Combat Log is now tucked behind a Show/Hide toggle instead of always taking up space
Arrows now have level requirements (Lucky: none, Iron: 32, Speed: 70) and are listed in that order in the Shop
Tightened up the Progression display
Fixed a crash that broke the entire game after logging in (Combat page's gold/EXP counters)
Added offline progress — your character keeps fighting whatever monster you last selected while you're away, capped at 2 hours, with a summary shown when you come back
Combat is now fully automatic — pick a monster from the zone roster and hit Fight, then watch it resolve itself with a live combat log, floating damage numbers, and gold/EXP ticking up
Gold and item drops grant instantly again on every kill, right in the combat log
Rare monsters now exist — 5% chance per kill, 2x HP, 5x gold/EXP, with a distinct glowing flourish
Replaced the isometric map and manual movement/combat with a tabbed layout: Combat, Equipment, Forge, Market, and Shop are now full pages instead of overlays on a game canvas
Added smooth animations throughout (HP bars, combat log entries, number count-ups) via Framer Motion
Gold and item drops now sit on the ground where an enemy died instead of going straight into your bag — walk or jump within 1 tile of a drop to automatically pick it up
Redesigned the side panel: an always-visible Equipment bar now sits at the top, your Character stats are tucked behind a collapsible panel, and your Inventory grid has much more room to show
Added an EXP bar along the bottom of the game view
Arrows can now be equipped with a right-click, in addition to selecting them and pressing Equip
Fixed item tooltips getting clipped near the edges of the Forge window
Composed items now show their tier right in the name, e.g. "Refined Wooden Sword (+1)"
Added Diablo/PoE-style hover tooltips for items, arrows, and stones — hover any tile in your Inventory, the Forge, or your equipped weapon to see its details
The Forge now shows your Inventory below the Upgrade Slot and Result Preview instead of squeezed in beside them
Composition feeding is now done through two fixed Fuel slots instead of an open-ended drop zone — drag in up to two stones or items at a time
Composition stones no longer stack — each one now takes up its own inventory slot, so 12 stones show as 12 separate tiles instead of one tile with a count
Feeding stones into the Forge is now one at a time per tile, matching how gear fuel already works
Composition stones now show up as draggable items in your Inventory instead of a typed-in quantity — drag a stone tile into the Forge's Fuel zone the same way you drag in gear
Added Composition — a third Forge upgrade path with guaranteed progress and no chance of failure

Feed stackable stones and/or sacrifice other gear as fuel to push an item toward its next +N tier, with a live progress bar showing exactly how far a feed would take you (even across multiple tiers at once)
Composition stones aren't dropped by anything yet — this is ready for testing once some are granted manually
Inventory is visible in the main side panel again, in addition to inside the Forge window
Redesigned the Forge with drag-and-drop: drag an item from your Inventory into the new Upgrade Slot to select it for upgrading
Added a live Result Preview showing exactly what your item would look like after a successful Quality or Level Upgrade, before you commit
Upgrade buttons now clearly explain why they're disabled (already maxed, or not enough currency) instead of just greying out
Inventory now lives inside the Forge window instead of the side panel
The Equipment panel's character placeholder is now a small isometric box matching your actual in-game character's look, instead of a plain rounded rectangle
The character placeholder in Equipment is now a segmented paper-doll showing Headgear/Body-Armor/Boots as color-coded bands and Weapon as a colored edge accent, tinted by item quality
Super-quality gear now gives its band/accent a slow, subtle glow
Rearranged the Equipment paper-doll: Head, Necklace, Ring, and Main Hand now stack down the right side, with Boots, Off-hand/Shield, and Armor lined up along the bottom
Fixed the new Equipment panel rendering with huge oversized slots and unnecessary scrollbars

Redesigned the Equipment panel into a paper-doll layout around a central character silhouette, with Weapon fully functional and Headgear/Boots/Necklace/Ring/Earring/Armor shown as locked placeholders for future gear types
Inventory is now always visible in the side panel instead of only while the Forge window is open
Fixed a crash that showed a brief flash of the character-select screen and then went blank after logging in
Arrow stacks now show up right in the main 40-slot Inventory grid alongside gear, instead of a separate list
Clicking a bottom-nav button (Zone/Equipment/Forge/Market/Shop) a second time now closes it
Removed the old class-switcher from the Stats panel — class is chosen once at character creation now
Character select now lists your characters in a single column
Inventory is now a fixed 40-slot grid, matching quality-colored tiles used in Equipment and the Forge — click a filled slot to see its details and equip it
If your inventory is full and you get a drop while playing, you'll now be asked to discard something to make room (or discard the new item) instead of it just failing silently
Zone, Equipment, Forge, and Market now only open from the bottom navigation bar as a window over the game view — they've been removed from the side panel
The side panel now only shows your Stats, plus your Inventory automatically while the Forge window is open
The Shop now sells arrows one full stack at a time (e.g. all 50 Lucky Arrows for one price) instead of one arrow at a time
The Shop now opens as a window over the game view instead of hiding the bottom navigation bar
Arrows are now a real stacked item — Lucky Arrows stack in groups of 50, Iron Arrows in 500, and Speed Arrows in 5000, shown right in your Inventory
You can now equip a specific stack of arrows from Inventory; a partially used stack stays untouched in your bag when you switch to a fresh one
Character creation now requires a name (capital letter first, lowercase after) that's unique across every account
Added the ability to delete a character from character select — you must type its name to confirm
Every new character now starts with 5,000 gold
Fixed the email confirmation link sometimes leading to an unreachable page (signing in afterward already worked regardless)
Added a Shop (new 5th button in the bottom nav) where Hunters can buy Iron, Lucky, and Speed arrows with gold
Hunters must now equip and manage arrows to attack — running out shows a clear warning until you restock
Added an arrow counter to the bottom-left of the game view for Hunter
Refreshing the page now resumes your last-played character instead of always returning to character select
Added character slots — each account can now have up to 5 characters, chosen from a new character-select screen after login
Your existing character and progress were automatically carried over as your first character slot
Creating a new character currently only offers Hunter; other classes show as locked
Gold, gear, and Forge currencies now belong to the specific character playing, not the account as a whole
Added a bottom navigation bar under the game view for quicker access to Zone, Equipment, Forge, and the new Marketplace tab
Forge upgrade costs now increase the further an item is upgraded, and show the real cost before you commit
Item quality now shows as a colored border and name prefix (e.g. "Refined Wooden Sword") across Inventory, Equipment, and Forge
Item drops now show a quality-colored name near where the enemy died — toggle it off in Settings > Display if you'd rather not see it
Added a Forge tab — spend DragonBalls to upgrade an item's quality, or Meteors to upgrade its level
Items now show their quality tier and level throughout Inventory, Equipment, and Forge
All upgrade rolls happen securely on the server so results can't be tampered with
Fixed item drops and inventory failing to load with a permission error
Backend hardening: closed an unused permission on item data ahead of future gear-upgrade features (no visible change)
Enemies now have a small chance to drop a weapon when defeated
Added Inventory and Equipment tabs — equip a dropped weapon to boost your Physical Attack
Equipped gear now saves and survives a refresh, just like the rest of your progress
Your class, level, gold, and EXP now save automatically and survive a page refresh or signing back in
New accounts start clean with sensible defaults instead of any risk of errors on first login
Actually fixed long jumps making tiles behind you vanish instantly instead of rippling out (the previous fix addressed the wrong cause)
Fixed long jumps across the map making tiles behind you vanish instantly instead of rippling out the way new tiles ripple in
Fixed a respawning monster occasionally appearing stuck at the edge of view instead of staying hidden until you're close enough to see it
Fixed tiles leaving view popping out instantly instead of fading out like they fade in
Monsters now fade in/out along with their tile instead of just appearing or vanishing
Spread each monster type across its entire quarter of the map, not just a small cluster near the start
Replaced monster HP numbers with health bars, plus a name label above each monster
Reorganized Twincross Outskirts so each monster type has its own area of the map
Added Display settings to toggle monster names and health bars on or off
Added the first real zone, Twincross Outskirts, with a small roster of enemies (Mudrat, Brushfowl, Fernvale Dove) scattered around the map instead of one single training dummy
Added HUD tabs to switch between Stats and Zone info, with Inventory and Equipment reserved for later
Killing enemies now grants Gold and EXP, shown in a new Progression panel
Added character leveling — gain levels as you earn EXP, with a level-up notification
Ranged classes (Hunter, Wuxia) can now attack from much farther away than melee classes
Click an enemy to auto-engage it — your hero walks over and keeps attacking until it dies
Initial project setup with sign-in and an isometric world to walk around in
Added the four classes (Hunter, Twin-soul, Wuxia, Juggernaut) with attribute-based stats
Added a first pass at combat: attack a nearby enemy and watch it take damage and fall
Added version tracking, a changelog, and What's New notifications
